title: OpenRTB in-page push bid via bid.ext text/desc/picture/favicon/click alias fields

source.name: ortbtools In-Page Push dialect contract (bid.ext alias field carrier)
source.notes: Exercises the dialect's documented per-role alias table (title: title/text; description: description/body/desc; image: image/image_url/picture; icon: icon/favicon; click: url/click/click_url/href/link) using the text/desc/picture/favicon/click spelling.

modifications: Wholly original OpenRTB envelope, imp, site, device and bid fields; only the field ROLE ALIASES (text/desc/picture/favicon/click) are taken from the dialect's own source comment.
IP uses TEST-NET-1 192.0.2.44; user/site identifiers are clearly synthetic fixture strings; asset/click/tracking URLs use reserved .test hostnames.
provenance.sanitized: No real visitor, publisher or advertiser data. IP 192.0.2.44 is TEST-NET-1; user.id/site.id are synthetic-fixture strings; every asset/click/tracking URL uses a reserved .test hostname.

device.ua: Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/120.0.0.0 Safari/537.36

ext.desc: See why commuters are switching routes this month.

specNotes: packages/core/dialects/inpage-push.js pickAlias(): title accepts title|text, description accepts description|body|desc, image accepts image|image_url|picture, icon accepts icon|favicon, click accepts url|click|click_url|href|link — this case exercises the text/desc/picture/favicon/click spelling from each list, first-present-wins.
claimsBid(bid) checks a title-ALIAS or image-ALIAS, not only the canonical key names; 'text' alone is enough to claim this bid, same as 'title' would be.

OpenRTB object-model requirements require at least one Banner, Video, Audio or Native object. A widget/zone extension alone does not satisfy that baseline requirement; imp.format_required is an expected error under both the IAB baseline and the current response-focused inpage-push dialect. The vendor format-tag/preview gap is separate from this correct diagnostic.
notes: Deliberately distinct from the sibling canonical-field case only in which alias name is used per role, so a Core regression in alias resolution shows up independently of the canonical path.

preview.limitation: Remote creative assets are blocked by the preview content policy.
